title: evaluatorStore has zero production writers; 5 readers show stale localStorage
body:
## Summary
src/stores/evaluatorStore.ts exposes setLastScan/addScanToHistory/setScanning but nothing in src, e2e or scripts calls them; five readers still render or route on its persisted lastScan/scanHistory.

## Description
Writers: zero (grep in evidence). Readers: src/components/modules/evaluator/CalendarRoadmapView/useCalendarRoadmapView.ts:21, src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/useHolisticHealthView.tsx:29, src/components/modules/evaluator/UnifiedSummaryView/useUnifiedSummaryView.ts:40, src/lib/nba-engine.ts:206, src/lib/event-bus-bridge.ts:111. The Scanner tab already moved to the durable projection (src/lib/evaluator/scan-report.ts scansToReports over evaluator_results; its header calls the old source "a store nothing writes"). The others read whatever an old build left in localStorage key pof-evaluator, or null forever. The bridge emits eval.scan.completed only when scanHistory.length grows, which never happens (no writer) and could not past 10 entries anyway (slice(-10) at src/stores/evaluatorStore.ts:27). Fixed = the readers take the useScannerFeed projection (or a shared server read) and the store is deleted, or the store is fed from deep-eval completion.

## Flow
- open Evaluator > Holistic Health / Unified Summary / Calendar Roadmap
- hook reads useEvaluatorStore.lastScan
- renders a localStorage leftover or "No scan" although evaluator_results holds scans
- fix: migrate the 5 readers onto scansToReports/useScannerFeed, then delete the store and its 6 test setState resets

## Expected impact
Evaluator summary views and the NBA engine stop reading a frozen cache; measured by writer count and a view test fed from evaluator_results. Risk: nba-engine ranking changes once it sees real scores.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - readers see the durable scan history instead of a store nothing writes
Before: 0 production writers, 5 production readers (grep 2026-11-08)
After: not taken - readers live in other contexts (veto 1)
Method: probe - grep of the writer/reader symbols; the migration is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
$ grep -rn "setLastScan\|addScanToHistory\|useEvaluatorStore.setState" src e2e scripts | grep -v src/stores/evaluatorStore.ts
-> only 6 test resets (setState({ lastScan: null })), 0 production writers
readers: src/components/modules/evaluator/CalendarRoadmapView/useCalendarRoadmapView.ts:21-22, src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/useHolisticHealthView.tsx:29-30, src/components/modules/evaluator/UnifiedSummaryView/useUnifiedSummaryView.ts:40, src/lib/nba-engine.ts:206, src/lib/event-bus-bridge.ts:111
impact: Evaluator summary views and the NBA engine stop reading a frozen cache; measured by writer count and a view test fed from evaluator_results. Risk: nba-engine ranking changes once it sees real scores.
instrument: a component test per reader seeding a mocked /api/evaluator/results and asserting the view shows that scan; writer grep 0 -> store deleted

title: Deep-eval POST without ueVersion starts a job whose every pass fails
body:
## Summary
src/app/api/evaluator/deep-eval/route.ts:39 defaults ueVersion to an empty string and src/lib/evaluator/deep-eval-job.ts:118 does the same; prompt assembly then throws "unsupported UE major version" for every pass, so the job settles completed with 100% failed passes.

## Description
buildDeepEvalPassPrompt -> buildProjectContextHeader -> getEngineFacts rejects an empty UE version. The engine catches it per pass as cli-error, so a request missing ueVersion is accepted (200), holds the project job slot, and settles completed with failedModules = every module. Observed this round: a job started without projectContext produced 4/4 passes cli-error "getEngineFacts: unsupported UE major version". Fixed = the route answers 400 when ueVersion is not a UE5 version (or the job refuses start), naming the field.

## Flow
- POST /api/evaluator/deep-eval { projectPath } with no ueVersion
- startDeepEvalJob -> runDeepEval -> buildDeepEvalPassPrompt throws per pass
- job completed, every pass error, nothing evaluated
- fix: validate ueVersion in the route before startDeepEvalJob

## Expected impact
A misconfigured caller gets a 400 naming the missing field instead of a completed scan that evaluated nothing. Risk: a caller relying on the default must now send ueVersion.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a request that cannot evaluate is refused, not run hollow
Before: 4/4 passes cli-error for a job with an empty ueVersion (observed while authoring src/__tests__/lib/evaluator/deep-eval-pass-ledger-guard.test.ts)
After: not taken - the route is outside this context's file_paths
Method: probe - one job run without ueVersion, statuses read from the snapshot
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A misconfigured caller gets a 400 naming the missing field instead of a completed scan that evaluated nothing. Risk: a caller relying on the default must now send ueVersion.
instrument: route test: POST without ueVersion -> expect 400 and getDeepEvalJob(project) === null

title: Deep-eval route runs paid passes for unknown module ids
body:
## Summary
The deep-eval POST accepts any non-empty string as a module id (src/app/api/evaluator/deep-eval/route.ts:28-30), while the batch-review route refuses unknown ids through resolveBatchModules (src/lib/evaluator/stale-review-plan.ts:37-53).

## Description
Two doors that spend CLI runs per module, two validation rules: batch-review names and refuses unknown ids; deep-eval forwards typos into 4 paid passes each with the generic checklist (or, before 08cfee1d, an inherited Object member's "undefined" checks). Fixed = deep-eval validates against the module universe (MODULE_LABELS / SubModuleId) in the resolveBatchModules shape, 400 naming the unknown ids.

## Flow
- POST /api/evaluator/deep-eval { projectPath, ueVersion, moduleIds: ["arpg-combt"] }
- job starts; 4 CLI passes run for a module that does not exist
- fix: resolve ids against the module universe, refuse the whole request on any unknown id

## Expected impact
Typos cost a 400 instead of four model calls. Risk: a caller using an id outside MODULE_LABELS is refused.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one refusal rule for every per-module paid door
Before: 1 of 2 per-module review doors validates ids (batch-review yes, deep-eval no)
After: 2 of 2 - not taken, route outside this context
Method: probe - read both routes' id handling
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/app/api/evaluator/deep-eval/route.ts:28  const moduleIds = Array.isArray(body.moduleIds) ? body.moduleIds.filter((m): m is string => typeof m === 'string' && m.length > 0) : undefined;
src/lib/evaluator/stale-review-plan.ts:48  return err(`Unknown or undefined module id(s): ${unknown.join(', ')}`);
impact: Typos cost a 400 instead of four model calls. Risk: a caller using an id outside MODULE_LABELS is refused.
instrument: route test: moduleIds ["nope"] -> 400 naming "nope", no job started

title: Cancel frees the deep-eval slot before the old passes settle
body:
## Summary
cancelDeepEvalJob sets status cancelled (src/lib/evaluator/deep-eval-job.ts:165) before awaiting the run, and startDeepEvalJob refuses only status running (line 96), so a start during the cancel window is accepted while up to 4 old CLI passes are still being killed.

## Description
The guard reads a status the cancel flips synchronously. Between the flip and the old run settling, a second POST starts a new job and jobs.set replaces the map entry, so up to 8 CLI processes run for one project and the old snapshot becomes unreachable. Fixed = refuse a start while the previous job's done promise is unsettled (a settled flag), or flip the status only after the run settles.

## Flow
- DELETE ?project=P while 4 passes are in flight
- status -> cancelled immediately; abort propagates asynchronously
- POST start for P is accepted before the old run settles
- fix: guard on an unsettled flag rather than on status

## Expected impact
One project never runs two deep-eval jobs at once. Risk: a start right after cancel gets 409 for a moment.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - at most one job in flight per project
Before: simulation: an executor that honours abort one tick late admits a second start (not run)
After: not taken
Method: simulation - walked the cancel/start ordering in deep-eval-job.ts; no harness this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/evaluator/deep-eval-job.ts:96  if (jobs.get(projectPath)?.snap.status === 'running') return err('already-running');
src/lib/evaluator/deep-eval-job.ts:164-167  job.snap.status = 'cancelled'; job.controller.abort(); await job.done.catch(() => undefined);
impact: One project never runs two deep-eval jobs at once. Risk: a start right after cancel gets 409 for a moment.
instrument: job test with an executor that rejects one macrotask after abort: cancel, start again without awaiting, assert the second start is refused and max concurrent executor calls <= 4

title: Pass ledger key omits project, so a reused scanId overwrites rows
body:
## Summary
deep_eval_passes is UNIQUE (scan_id, module_id, pass) (src/lib/evaluator/deep-eval-pass-ledger.ts:33) and recordPassOutcome upserts on that key, so a second project running with the same scanId overwrites the first project's recorded passes.

## Description
Commit 79c73b62 scopes READS to the project; the WRITE key still lacks project_id, so project B's run of scanId X replaces project A's rows of X and A can no longer resume. Fixed = UNIQUE (scan_id, project_id, module_id, pass) via the table-rebuild procedure scan-findings-db.ts already uses, or server-minted scan ids a client cannot reuse across projects.

## Flow
- project A records scan X passes
- POST start for project B with scanId X
- B's passes upsert over A's rows
- A resumes X -> its passes are gone

## Expected impact
Resume never loses another project's finished passes. Risk: a table rebuild on an existing DB.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - recorded passes survive a scanId collision
Before: simulation: 1 key collision overwrites 1 row per (module, pass)
After: not taken
Method: simulation - read the DDL and upsert; schema rebuild kept out of an unattended round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/evaluator/deep-eval-pass-ledger.ts:33  UNIQUE (scan_id, module_id, pass)
src/lib/evaluator/deep-eval-pass-ledger.ts:45  ON CONFLICT (scan_id, module_id, pass) DO UPDATE SET
impact: Resume never loses another project's finished passes. Risk: a table rebuild on an existing DB.
instrument: in-memory DB test: record (X, A) then (X, B) for the same cell; assert readPassLedger(X, A) still returns its row

title: buildEvalPrompt takes a moduleName it never uses
body:
## Summary
EvalPromptParams.moduleName is destructured and unused in src/lib/evaluator/module-eval-prompts.ts:427 (the file's one lint warning); deep-eval-engine computes and passes it anyway.

## Description
src/lib/evaluator/deep-eval-engine.ts:42 derives moduleName = projectName || MyProject to build sourcePath, then passes it to buildEvalPrompt, which ignores it and prints projectName raw (an empty name renders as UE5 project ""). Fixed = drop the field from EvalPromptParams and its callers, or use it on the project line so an empty name reads the same fallback the source path uses.

## Flow
- eslint src/lib/evaluator/module-eval-prompts.ts -> 1 warning no-unused-vars moduleName
- fix: remove the param (type + call sites) or use it in the header line

## Expected impact
One fewer misleading parameter; the eval header stops printing an empty project name. Risk: none beyond the call sites.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - prompt params mean what they say
Before: 1 lint warning; 1 unused param passed by 1 caller
After: 0 - not taken (touches deep-eval-engine.ts, unowned)
Method: gate - eslint on the file
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/lib/evaluator/module-eval-prompts.ts:427:40 warning 'moduleName' is assigned a value but never used @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars
impact: One fewer misleading parameter; the eval header stops printing an empty project name. Risk: none beyond the call sites.
instrument: eslint warning count on module-eval-prompts.ts 1 -> 0 plus a prompt-content assertion for an empty projectName

title: 18 feature-defined modules are evaluated with 3 generic checks only
body:
## Summary
MODULE_CONTEXTS covers 16 modules; 18 modules that MODULE_FEATURE_DEFINITIONS tracks (models, animations, level-design, ui-hud, physics, multiplayer, save-load, input-handling, packaging, ...) fall back to a 3-line generic checklist per pass.

## Description
getPassChecks (src/lib/evaluator/module-eval-prompts.ts:463) returns three generic bullets when a module has no context. A deep eval over those modules grades them against file organisation / UE5 conventions / Tick usage only. Authoring their criteria is prompt CONTENT, so it is a direction call: which of the 18 deserve a dedicated context, and in what order.

## Flow
- probe: getEvaluableModuleIds() = 16; Object.keys(MODULE_FEATURE_DEFINITIONS) minus those = 18
- deep eval of e.g. physics uses the generic fallback
- operator decides which modules get authored criteria

## Expected impact
Deep-eval findings for the 18 modules become domain-specific. Risk: new criteria change those modules' scores.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every tracked module evaluated against its own criteria
Before: 16 of 34 feature-defined modules have a context (probe 2026-11-08)
After: unmeasured - content authoring
Method: probe - enumerated both registries in a scratch vitest
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
impact: Deep-eval findings for the 18 modules become domain-specific. Risk: new criteria change those modules' scores.
